name: Referrals and correspondence sent by a clinician
one_line: The organizational situation of a clinician's OUTBOUND letter file: referrals made, clinic and discharge letters written to other clinicians, replies received against them, reports issued to third parties on a patient's behalf, and the register that tracks whether each one was sent and answered. Absorbs the legacy row med.clinician-referral-sent. The organizing anchor is the correspondence ITEM and its direction of address, not the patient's accumulated record. Gist-level placeholder (J-IND); it writes NO field rows, because the clinical_practice schema declares none.

deterministic: PRECONDITION: every entry is a DETECTION signal, never an extraction licence - this template's schema declares no field rows. “Privacy policy must be enforced before content reaches any model or external connector.”

an outbound-letter structure: an addressee block naming a clinician, service, or practice OTHER than the holder; a labelled re or subject block naming a THIRD person with a date of birth or record-number token; a body; and a sign-off naming the holder. Three distinct person-shaped roles in three labelled positions is the shape, and the direction of address is the discriminating evidence.

a referral-form structure: a labelled referred-by slot, a referred-to service slot, a reason-for-referral section, an urgency or pathway designation, and an attached-information list. The urgency designation is a raw observation from a source system and never becomes this product's classification.
a copied-to structure: a distribution or cc block listing further recipients including, often, the patient - which is what makes one letter a correspondence item rather than a chart entry.

a reply-pairing structure: a letter whose own header quotes the reference or date of an earlier referral, or an acknowledgement carrying an appointment offer against a named referral. Reply chains are the register's own join.

a third-party report structure: an insurer, employer, school, court, or benefits agency as addressee, a consent-obtained line, and a factual-report body about a patient - issued by the clinician at someone's request.

an email whose labelled recipient slot resolves to a clinical or secure-messaging domain and whose labelled subject slot names a third person's referral or case, with the holder in the sender slot. The addressing direction is what fires; source_type contributes only as a file-kind signal.

a correspondence-register structure: a repeated log-row shape of date, subject, addressee, kind, and a sent or acknowledged status. “Tables matter because resumes, forms, applications, invoices, and administrative documents often place their most useful information in cells rather than body paragraphs.”
needs_llm: PRECONDITION: patient-identifying by default; any model step runs after P7 and under the user's policy. “Protected material should not be included in cloud-model prompts by default, should not display raw content in general group summaries, and should not be moved automatically without a user policy that explicitly permits it.”
an unlabelled letter - prose with a greeting and a sign-off and no blocks, or a scanned dictated letter with no recoverable structure.

distinguishing an outbound clinical letter from an INBOUND one the holder received about their own care, when both carry a clinician sign-off and a patient block and the holder's name appears in each - the central determination for this row. The model must abstain rather than assert: “A model that cannot cite sufficient evidence must return unknown.”
distinguishing a real letter from a template, an exemplar, a portfolio sample, or a completed teaching exercise reproducing the letter structure.

separating a clinical referral from an administrative onward-send - a records request, a chase, an invoice covering letter - that shares the addressee-and-patient shape. “Topic answers what a file is about, while purpose answers what the file was for.”
never_alone: letter structure alone - an addressee, a greeting, a body, and a sign-off describe every letter ever written, and this is the tempting false file for this row.
referral vocabulary alone. Referral appears in guidance, in policy, in marketing, in recruitment, and in a patient's own copy of a letter about them.
a clinician name in an addressee or sign-off block alone, including in a PDF author or producer string - “PDF metadata should be treated as supporting evidence, not as truth”

a facility gazetteer hit alone, read across from “A university name alone should not create a group because Columbia can appear as an authoring school, course provider, target institution, employer, research venue, or merely a cited organization.” by inference.
a bare 4-digit number read as a record number, a referral number, or a year.
source_type = email alone, and extension alone. 00: “treat the file extension as a routing signal rather than an assumption about meaning”
a parent folder named Letters, Referrals, or Sent alone.
membership in a download session that dropped a batch of letters out of one practice system - “A session should never be treated as proof of topic”
a copied-to line naming the patient, read as proof the patient is the holder.

work_types: referral letter or referral form sent
reply or acknowledgement received against a referral
report issued to an insurer, employer, school, or agency
certificate or fitness statement issued about a patient
correspondence register, sent log, or chase list
grouping_reasons: one referral and everything answering it: the letter sent, the acknowledgement, the appointment offer, the reply letter - joined by an exact reference or a quoted date rather than by similar filenames. Membership copies nothing - “The graph does not automatically copy those missing facts onto sparse files.”
one correspondence item across its versions: dictation, typed draft, verified letter, signed and sent copy, joined by the universal version_family fact.
one subject's outgoing letters over time - a real reason to group and the one most likely to tempt a subject label onto members, which must not happen.
one third-party report and the request, consent, and invoice around it - purpose-coherent while content-incoherent: “The documents are content-incoherent but purpose-coherent.”
no group at all is a valid outcome; a single sent letter is still protected material.

template.why: Empty by binding contract and by privacy. By contract: clinical_practice declares no fields, so no dimension can branch (D1 as narrowed, _CONTRACT rules 10 and 15, PR-6). By privacy: the anchors this situation wants are a patient and a receiving service, and both publish third-party information as folder LABELS - a service name in a branch discloses what a named person is being investigated for almost as directly as a diagnosis would. “Protected branches should have configurable redaction in the canvas and review screens”. The present recommendation is one shallow, redacted, user-approved correspondence packet with no automatic internal depth. Held as prose: if fields ever land, the correspondence direction (sent versus received) and then the document function is the recorded starting recommendation, because direction is the property this situation is actually organized by and it discloses nothing about any patient. A subject level would remain off by default. Not time-first - “For document and record domains, project, function, or subject usually comes before time because putting year first scatters related work across calendar folders.”.

collides_with.signal: The reciprocal of the chart row's own entry, and the sharpest overlap inside this family: every letter this row holds is also filed into a chart, frequently as a byte-identical copy that the universal duplicate_family fact will join. The discriminating evidence: an addressee block, a copies-to distribution, a sent or acknowledged status, or a reply pairing supports this row; the same letter sitting inside ONE subject's accumulated dated record, under a filed-on slot, supports the chart row. The letter's own body discriminates nothing, and where both readings hold the correct outcome is to let P10 choose from an accepted group rather than to force one here. Provenance: inference.

The clinician-authored versus patient-held boundary in its most confusable form, because appointment letters, clinic letters, and discharge letters are physically the SAME documents on both sides - the patient is routinely copied in. The discriminating evidence: the holder in the sign-off or referred-by block, with a differently named subject, supports this row; the holder in the patient or re slot, or second-person prose addressed to the holder, supports medical.personal-health-records. Letterhead, headings, and record numbers discriminate neither. AUTHORED ONE-WAY HERE: the landed medical.personal-health-records node does not name clinical_practice, and R1c owes the reciprocal - see this row's memo (NJ-CP-1). Provenance: inference.

A clinician's report issued to an insurer, employer, or agency for a fee has an addressee, a scope, a factual body, and a fee note, which is also the shape of a consulting deliverable. The discriminating evidence: a named patient with a consent line, and clinical content about that person, supports this row; a client engagement anchor - a signed statement of work, a commercial scope - supports the consulting row. A fee note supports neither. Provenance: inference.

Administrative onward-sends - records requests, chases, invoice covering letters - carry the addressee-and-patient shape without being clinical correspondence. The discriminating evidence: a clinical reason-for-referral or clinical body content supports this row; a purely procedural request about a record rather than about care supports administration. Provenance: inference.

falls_through_to.why: The primary home for a recognised letter, referral, reply, or register when no accepted correspondence group or approved branch exists. “Protected Records may represent sensitive isolated material such as passport scans, medical documents, account statements, visas, legal forms, or credentials; it should normally remain local-only and must not cause filenames or content to be exposed in model prompts.”

The cautious outcome for a letter-shaped document whose direction of address and subject role stay unresolved. “Review Later may hold files whose meaning is partly understood but whose final location requires a future decision.”

The safe outcome for an untranscribed dictation or an encrypted correspondence export. “Unsupported or Encrypted may hold—or, more safely, represent without moving—password-protected archives, unreadable documents, damaged files, and unknown formats.”

The home for a standalone letter template or blank referral form carrying no subject at all. “Independent Records may live under Personal/Independent Records and hold standalone certificates, notices, confirmations, forms, and PDFs that have a durable purpose but no broader group.”

The inactive home for referral guidance, pathway documents, and service directories with no case attached. “Reading Inbox may hold papers, articles, reports, and saved PDFs that appear to be reading material but have no active research, course, or project association.”

sensitivity_why: A clinical letter is unusually disclosive for its size: the addressee service alone can reveal what a named person is being investigated for, before a single body line is read, and the same file names a referring clinician, a receiving clinician, and a patient together. 00 names the material - the corpus “can include identity documents, account statements, tax records, medical information, legal records, credentials, private correspondence, GPS metadata, employment materials, and educational records.” - and requires the immediate transition: “A scanned passport, tax statement, medical document, authentication key, or account record should enter a protected state immediately.”. The operative limits are 00's: “Protected material should not be included in cloud-model prompts by default, should not display raw content in general group summaries, and should not be moved automatically without a user policy that explicitly permits it.”. The disclosive-addressee point is stated as inference, not as a 00 claim. This row assigns only the catalogue value potentially_sensitive; it does not assign, alias, rank, or infer a P7 handling class.
open_question: Whether this row and clinical_practice.patient-chart should remain two rows. They pass the node test today on genuinely different detection signals (direction of address and a sent-or-answered register, versus longitudinal accumulation about one subject) and on a different organizing anchor, and a real clinician keeps a sent-letters file that is not the chart. But the SAME letter is routinely in both, often byte-identical, so a large fraction of files will legitimately evidence both rows and neither has dimensions today. This row's position is that they should stay two, because the correspondence register is a workflow the chart does not contain - but the question belongs to R1c with the whole family in view, not to this row alone. A second, narrower fork for R1c: whether a clinician's report issued to a third party for a fee is correspondence at all, or a deliverable that belongs with practice administration.
